questions.question: Dimensional formula of Pressure?
questions.solution:
__CONCEPT____:__

__
 
• Pressure: The force per unit area is called pressure. It is denoted by P.
 
• The SI unit of pressure is the pascal (Pa).
 
• The basic formula for pressure is given by:

{{Pressure (P)}} = frac{{{{Force (F)}}}}{{{{Area (A)}}}}

EXPLANATION__:

The pressure is defined as force per unit area i.e.

P = (F)/(A)

As force = mass × acceleration

acceleration = velocity × time⁻¹ = [L T-1] [T]-1 = [L T-2]

∴ The dimensional formula of force = [M] × [L T-2]

⇒ Force = M1 L1 T-2

​⇒ The dimensional formula of area = M0 L2 T0

 
• Hence the dimensional formula of pressure is

P = (F)/(A) = frac{{ML{T ⁻ ²}}}{{{L²}}} = M{L ⁻ ¹}{T ⁻ ²}

questions.question: 152° Fahrenheit is equal to ______ °Celsius.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__66.67__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

The formula to convert Celsius to Fahrenheit is given:-

 
• F = °C × (9/5) + 32 
 
• Hence 
 
• (F-32) div {9over 5} = C° 

 
• F = [ C × (9/5) + 32 ] 

 
• Given that, F = 152° 

 
• C° = (F-32) div {9over 5} 
 
• C° = (152-32) times {5over9}
 
• **C° = 66.67**

questions.question: The dimensional symbol LT ⁻² represents which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option **'3'.**

__**Concept:**__

**Dimensional formulas or symbols:**

 
• It is an expression showing the powers to which the fundamental units are to be raised to obtain one unit of derived quantity.
 
• If 'X' be any physical quantity, then expression representing its dimensional formula is given by

**X⁼ M^aL^bT^c**

Where M, L, T are base dimensions m

questions.question: A certain household has consumed 320 units of energy during a month. How much energy is this in joules?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3) 1152 x 10⁶ J.

To convert from units of energy (kWh) to joules, we use the formula:

1 kWh = 3.6 x 10⁶ J

So, 320 units of energy is:

320 kWh x 3.6 x 10⁶ J/kWh = 1.152 x 10⁹ J

Therefore, the answer is **1152 x 10⁶ J.**

questions.question: To represent the speed of 72 kmh⁻¹ in ms⁻¹, we will write ________.

questions.question: What is the dimensional formula for the universal gravitational constant ?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

__
 
• The **dimensional formula** is a compound expression showing how and which of the fundamental quantities are involved in making that physical quantity.
 
• Some denotation of fundamental quantities
 
 
• Mass - M
 
• Distance - L
 
• Time - T
 
• Temperature - K
 
• Electric Current - A
 
 

**Calculation:**__

Force = G × m₁ × m₂ × [r²]⁻¹

⇒ G = Force × r² × [m₁ × m₂]⁻¹ --- (1)

Where, G = Universal Gravitational Constant

Now, the dimensions of,

Mass = [M¹ L⁰ T⁰] --- (2)

Radius (distance) = [M⁰ L¹ T⁰] --- (3)

Force = [M¹ L¹ T⁻²] --- (4)

On substituting equation (2), (3) and (4) in equation (1) we get,

Universal Gravitational Constant = Force × r² × [m₁ × m₂]⁻¹

⇒ G = [M¹ L¹ T⁻²] × [M⁰ L¹ T⁰]² × [M¹ L⁰ T⁰]⁻¹ × [M¹ L⁰ T⁰]⁻¹ = [M⁻¹ L³ T⁻²].

**Therefore, the Universal Gravitational Constant is dimensionally represented as [M⁻¹ L³ T⁻²].**

questions.question: The temperature of a substance increases by 27°C. On the Kelvin scale this increase is -
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**27 K**__.

__**Concept:**__

**Celsius scale**

__
 
• The **Celsius temperature scale** is also known as the **Centigrade temperature scale** because it divides the boiling and freezing points of water by 100 degrees.
 
• The Celsius temperature scale is **used to measure temperatures all over the world.**
 
• The** temperatures on this scale **are all in **°C **(degree celsius).

**Kelvin scale**

 
• The **Kelvin temperature scale **is also known as the **thermodynamic scale.**
 
• The Kelvin scale was designed in such a way that the z**ero point of the temperature scale is set at absolute zero. **
 
• As a result, **the absolute zero is 0 K. **
 
• The Kelvin temperature scale is** widely used in scientific calculations and equations** because it has a direct relationship with absolute zero.
 
• The** temperatures on this scale** are in **K **(Kelvin).

**Calculation**__:

**The relation between Kelvin and Celsius scale can be written as:**

T (K) = T (°C) + 273

Let T₁ = a₁ °C = (a₁ + 273) K

 T₂ = a₂ °C = (a₂ + 273) K

Change in temperature:

⇒ T₂ - T₁ = (a₂ - a₁)°C = (a₂ - a₁) K

__**Temperature change in Celsius scale = Temperature change in Kelvin scale = 27 K**__

questions.question: The force (F) acting on a body varies with displacement x as F = ax² + bx + c. Find the dimensional formula of b. (a, b and c are constants).
questions.solution:
__CONCEPT__**:**

__
 
• Principle of homogeneity of dimensions: According to this principle, a physical equation will be dimensionally correct if the dimensions of all the terms occurring on both sides of the equation are the same.

 
 
• This principle is based on the fact that only the physical quantities of the same kind can be added, subtracted, or compared.
 
• Thus, the velocity can be added to velocity but not to force.
 
 

EXPLANATION__**:**

Given that:

F = ax2 + bx + c

 
• From the principle of dimensional homogeneity, the left-hand side of the equation dimensionally equal to the right-hand side of the equation.

The dimensional formula of Force (F) = [M L T⁻²]

The dimensional formula of Displacement (x) = [L]

LHS = RHS

[M L T-2] = [b] × [L]

[b] = M L⁰ T⁻²

Hence option 4 is correct.

questions.question: How many dynes are equal to 1 Newton ?
questions.solution:
The correct option is **10⁵.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Force: The interaction that after applying to a body changes or try to change the state of motion or state of rest is called force.
 
• Force is denoted by F and the SI unit is Newton (N).
 
• 
 
Force (F) = Mass (m) × acceleration (a)

 
 
• Both Dyne and Newton are units of force in the CGS and S.I systems.
 
• Newton and dyne can also be written as (1 N = kg-m/s2) and (1 dyne = gm-cm/s2).

⇒ 1 dyne = 1 gm-cm/s2 and 1 newton = 1 kg-m/s2

⇒ 1 kg = 1000 gm.

⇒ 1 m = 100 cm.

⇒ 1 kg-m/s2 = 1000 gm × 100 cm/s2 ⇒ 105 gm-cm/s2 = 105 dyne.

⇒ 1 dyne = 10-5 kg-m/s2 ⇒ 10-5 N

⇒ 1 N = 105 dyne

⇒ 1 dyne = 10-5 N

questions.question: The dimensional formula ML²T⁻² may NOT correspond to:
questions.solution:
__**CONCEPT:**__

__
 
• Dimensional Formula: The dimensions of a physical quantity represent its nature. 
 
• ​Dimensional Formula can help us in finding the relationship between different physical quantities.
 
 
• For example, Dimensional Formula for work done and Kinetic Energy is the same. So, we can say they are related.
 
 
 
• For dimensionless quantities, dimensional analysis can't be possible.
 
 
• For example, Relative density is a dimensionless quantity which is the ratio of two densities. we cannot find the dimension of relative density
 
 
 
• The dimension of fundamental quantities are known and dimensional formulas for other quantities are derived from fundamental units.

 

**​EXPLANATION:**__

Given dimension formula: ML2T-2

Torque = Force × radius = Nm = ML2T-2

Energy = Work = Force × distance = Nm = ML2T-2

Momentum = Mass × velocity = kg-m/sec = MLT-1

Hence, The dimensional formula ML2T-2 is NOT correspond to momentum
